text:
Nina: dropped a quick review of the latest compare-table prototypes. main concerns: visual noise from stacked badges, unclear pin scope, and filter labeling that confuses new users. figma: https://figma.redwood/compare-new

Omar: nice direction. main +1 on simplifying badges. i think we should avoid full solid fills for perf badges in the table row — too demanding on attention. :sparkles:

Priya: pinning question — are pins tied to the user or the workspace by default? current mock implies workspace-level, which could surprise folks who expect their personal view.

Nina: leaning user-default, with an explicit “Make this visible to workspace” toggle in the pin menu. we should surface that option for power users but keep common case simple.

Evan: accessibility: chips currently use small 11px white text on colored backgrounds; contrast checks failing for amber/green. we should either increase font weight/size or switch to dark text for lighter chips. AccessibilityBot can confirm numbers.

AccessibilityBot: automated check results: chip-amber #FFB84D on white text -> contrast 2.6:1 (fails). recommended fixes: a) dark text #4A2F00, b) add 1px stroke, or c) use outlined chip with dark border and dark text.

Priya: copy micro-tweak: filter currently labeled "Model family/signature" which bundles unrelated concepts. suggest splitting to "Architecture" and "Signature" or using "Family" with a tooltip. users get confused between model family and model size.

Omar: table density option idea: keep a default compact mode for power users (shows compact chips only) and a comfy mode where badges expand into full labels and descriptions. persist per-user.

Nina: agree. additionally, show a legend toggle — small ? icon that expands a legend panel explaining badge thresholds (p50 latency bands) and pin semantics. make legend dismissible and keyboard accessible.

Evan: hover behavior: badges expand on hover after 150ms; keyboard users need same reveal on focus. also please respect reduce-motion and allow instant reveal for keyboard.

Priya: pin microcopy: change from "Pinned: v3" to "Pinned for you — v3" and when org-level pin add "Pinned for workspace — v3". avoids ambiguity in multi-collab pages.

Omar: small visual suggestion: use thinner outline chips with left icon for type (perf, cost, accuracy) so rows read left-to-right instead of stacked colored blocks. will mock in a few iterations.

AccessibilityBot: also flagged that badge tooltip uses role="tooltip" but not tied to aria-describedby on the triggering button. recommend adding aria-describedby and ensuring tooltip is accessible via keyboard only when focused.

Nina: decision candidates: 1) switch chips to outlined variant with dark text to pass contrast, 2) implement per-user density toggle (compact/comfy) with persisted preference, 3) pin default = per-user with optional org toggle and clearer microcopy, 4) legend panel explaining perf thresholds and pin scope. any objections?

Priya: no objections. i'll update the copy and add tooltip text for the legend explaining p50 thresholds and link to docs.

Omar: i'll push a compact mock with outlined chips + icon and show how hover expands. will include motion-reduced variant.

Evan: i'll validate the outlined chips for color contrast and tab order. will post an a11y checklist and quick keyboard walkthrough.

Nina: timeline: mock updates by EOD, copy and a11y checklist by tomorrow morning. let's reconvene async once prototypes are posted. thanks! :thumbsup:

AccessibilityBot: reminder: submit updated tokens for chip states to /shared/design-tokens when ready.

Nina: keeping thread open until mocks + checks are in.
